title: Building Bridges – AI Custom Chatbots as Mediators between Mathematics and Physics
extended_summary:
This paper examines whether learning materials generated by a custom AI chatbot can improve sixth-grade students’ learning experience and performance when studying proportional relationships across mathematics and physics. The authors focus on a common transfer problem in STEM education: students often struggle to move from mathematical representations to physical meaning, such as interpreting tables, graphs, and formulas in a physics context.

The intervention was a custom GPT configured in OpenAI with course- and age-appropriate prompts and supporting knowledge. In the experimental condition, students received a textbook overview plus an AI-generated explanation; the control group received the same overview plus traditional textbook examples. The comparison was conducted as a randomized controlled study with 214 sixth-grade students in German secondary schools, using paper-based materials over a 15-minute learning phase followed by immediate questionnaires and a performance test.

Results showed no significant overall advantage for the AI condition on learning performance, but the AI-generated explanations significantly improved positive-activating emotions, situational interest, self-efficacy, and reduced intrinsic and extrinsic cognitive load. For transfer-related performance, findings were mixed: one subtask favored the AI group, while others favored the textbook group, and the overall performance test did not differ significantly. The authors conclude that custom chatbots may enhance the learning experience, but their impact on achievement and transfer remains unclear and needs further study.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a randomized controlled trial with direct comparison to a non-AI textbook baseline and a clearly defined intervention and outcome set. Credibility is strong, but the brief, single-topic field implementation and some non-significant/mixed performance findings limit certainty and broader generalizability.
impact_tier_rationale: The study reports small-to-medium positive effects on learner experience outcomes (d≈0.45-0.63), which are meaningful but modest. Academic performance impact is mixed and overall non-significant, so the practical educational impact appears limited to moderate at present.

interventions.use_case: custom GPT-based chatbot generating age-appropriate explanations for proportional relationships, including graphs, tables, and formulas, to support sixth-grade mathematics/physics learning

finding.finding_summary: In a randomized controlled study with N=214 sixth-grade students, AI-generated explanations improved one transfer-related performance subtask but did not improve the overall achievement test. The experimental group outperformed the control group on subtask C (calculating the constant of proportionality) with a small effect (d=0.32, p=0.022), while the control group did better on two values within subtask B (values 3 and 5; d=0.33 and d=0.29), and the overall test score was non-significant (p=0.750).
finding.measure: Performance test on proportional relationships in a physics context; overall score and subtasks A-D, including transfer/mathematization tasks
finding.effect_size: d=0.32 (subtask C); d=0.33 and d=0.29 (subtask B values 3 and 5); overall not_reported

finding.finding_summary: The AI-generated explanations improved several learner experience measures in the randomized controlled study (N=214). Compared with textbook materials, the experimental group reported higher positive-activating emotions (d=0.48, p=0.00093), higher situational interest (d=0.45, p=0.00223), higher self-efficacy (d=0.63, p=0.00001), and lower intrinsic and extrinsic cognitive load (d=0.47 and d=0.59, respectively).
finding.measure: Positive-activating emotions, situational interest, intrinsic cognitive load, extrinsic cognitive load, self-efficacy expectations
